summary: Session S3 definitively confirmed the root cause: interval_nf_types (Finset of 1-var NFs) is semantically too weak for sub-interval matching. The splitting lemma (deriving sub-interval types from full-interval types + endpoint NFs) is PROVABLY FALSE via concrete counterexample. Additionally identified that the formula-level encoding (nf_exist_sf_guarded) uses a trivially-true guard that cannot constrain intermediate point types, making the backward direction (sorry at line 2775) also unfixable without formula restructuring. All three sorries (2335, 2417, 2775) share the same root cause and require a coordinated formula-level + bridge-lemma fix.

blocking_issues.description: Three interconnected sorries (2335, 2417, 2775) share the same root cause: interval_nf_types loses spatial information. The splitting lemma is provably false. The formula guard is trivially true. Both need coordinated restructuring.
blocking_issues.root_cause: 1) interval_nf_types records a SET of types, not spatial arrangement. Sub-interval types are NOT derivable. 2) nf_exist_sf_guarded uses interval_guard_sf which is trivially true (every point satisfies some NF), providing no constraint on intermediate point types. The backward direction cannot extract bridge lemma hypotheses from the formula.
blocking_issues.splitting_lemma_disproof: Counterexample: M has types [A, B] in (x,t) with A in (x,u) and B in (u,t). M' has same types but B in (x',u') and A in (u',t'). Same interval_nf_types, same endpoint NFs, but different sub-interval types.

D_formula_restructuring.description: RECOMMENDED. Modify nf_exist_sf_guarded to encode the interval type configuration in the formula itself. Replace trivially-true interval_guard_sf with a config-specific guard. The formula becomes a disjunction over all valid (witness_nf, interval_type_set) configurations. Forward direction: extract actual config from nf_eval_nf. Backward direction: extract config from formula truth, apply bridge lemma with extracted config as bridge data. This is the GHR93 decomposition formula approach adapted to our NF framework.
D_formula_restructuring.risk: MEDIUM. The bridge lemma proof (nf_fraisse_compression + nf_2var_existential_transfer) may need its hypotheses strengthened to accept the config data. The transfer might then need the config for sub-intervals, which the config-based approach CAN provide because the config is part of the formula structure, not derived from model theory.

A_directional_splitting.description: REJECTED in S3. The splitting lemma is provably false. No variation of directional 2-var NF extraction can recover sub-interval types from the set-based interval_nf_types.

B_richer_invariant.description: Replace interval_nf_types with richer structure. Viable but more invasive than D. Requires updating all 27 references to interval_nf_types in StaviCompleteness.lean.

C_ef_game.description: Full EF game formalization. Most principled but most infrastructure.

key_discoveries: Splitting lemma is PROVABLY FALSE (not just hard to prove)
interval_guard_sf is trivially true and provides no constraint
The formula-level fix (Option D) is the only approach that fixes ALL three sorries simultaneously
Variable dropping lemma (from S2) is valid and useful for the formula-level fix

next_action_hint: Implement Option D (formula restructuring): 1) Add config_guard formula that constrains interval types, 2) Modify nf_exist_sf_guarded to disjoin over configs, 3) Re-prove forward direction, 4) Prove backward direction using config as bridge data, 5) Modify nf_2var_existential_transfer to accept config parameter.
